Negative Appraisals.value: I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible
I have permanently changed for the worse
I can't stop bad things from happening to me

vignette: Jared is a 22-year-old African male and school principal who has been experiencing significant psychological distress following his traumatic childhood experiences of physical abuse by a caregiver. He recently sought help after struggling with increasingly debilitating symptoms that have affected both his personal life and professional responsibilities. Growing up, Jared was subjected to intense physical abuse that left him feeling overwhelmed and helpless. The unpredictability and intensity of these episodes continue to haunt him today. Unpredictable situations, old photos, and waking up from nightmares are potent triggers for Jared’s distress. When he encounters these triggers, they bring back fragmented memories that feel more real than any ordinary recollection. For example, finding an old photo in his parents’ home can immediately transport him back to a moment of intense pain and fear, where the details of the abuse come flooding back but remain disconnected, like pieces of a puzzle that don’t fit together. These vivid flashes of memory are often overwhelming and make it difficult for him to recall events deliberately or piece them together in a coherent narrative. Jared’s fears about his own anger have grown over time. He is certain that he will not be able to control his rage, which has led him to avoid situations where he might lose control. This fear of rage has been exacerbated by the belief that he has permanently changed for the worse and that he remains helplessly vulnerable to bad things happening to him. These negative appraisals feed into each other, creating a cycle of distress. His sense of helplessness is reinforced by his fragmented memories, which make it hard for him to see himself as anything but damaged and fragile. When he tries to deliberately recall what happened during the abuse, the difficulty in accessing these memories only strengthens his belief that something inside him has been permanently altered. These negative appraisals also intensify his reaction to triggers. For instance, waking up from a nightmare leaves him feeling more helpless and angry than ever, leading to further fragmented recollections of past events. This cycle has led Jared to avoid certain situations at work and home, which in turn has strained his relationship with his partner. His avoidance behaviors have had concrete consequences. At work, he finds it increasingly difficult to manage unpredictable situations that could arise during a school day, such as emergencies or conflicts among students. His difficulty in handling these moments has affected his performance and left him feeling even more helpless and frustrated. The distress has become so overwhelming that Jared finally decided to seek help. He is most afraid of losing control and hurting someone, but he also hopes to find ways to manage his memories and negative thoughts so that they do not dictate how he lives his life anymore. Jared’s story highlights the intertwined nature of his triggers, fragmented memories, and negative appraisals, which have collectively created a distressing cycle that has significantly impacted his daily functioning.
